text:
Elaine Walker: Quick sync — thinking we spin a short "snackable" tutorial loop (3 x ~7min videos + blog + sample app) aimed at engineers who want to prototype Redwood inference in a day. Goal: low friction, measurable demo, clear CTA for self-serve credits and webinar sign-up.

Marco Chen: love that. Can we pair each tutorial with a tiny benchmark narrative? e.g., 1) latency-focused local dev, 2) cost-focused batching tips, 3) private deploy checklist. Each has one chart + one short takeaway.

Priya Nair: agree. For distribution: short carousel posts, one long-form medium-style blog, and an optional live workshop/webinar that walks through the sample app. Webinar = gated, funnel to SDRs.

Samir Patel: Funnel/lead routing note — gated webinar signups should tag source=snackable-tutorials, utm_campaign=snackloop, and pass model preference on form. That way we can route high-model-usage leads to AE queue.

Dana Ortiz: copy angle suggestion: "Build an LLM feature in a day — with predictable latency and lower cost". Keep it developer-forward, include a small code snippet in the blog showing the API call.

Elaine Walker: good. Draft social copy idea: `Try the 1-day prototype: 3 bite-sized tutorials + sample app. Get $100 credits to deploy on Redwood. Sign up -> link` — we should A/B headline vs "Prototype LLM features in hours."

Marco Chen: can we get a tiny benchmarking script included in the repo? Something like:```bash
# run simple latency test
python tools/bench_latency.py --model redwood-3b --seq 128 --n 50
```

Priya Nair: timeline? I can take the blog + webinar outline. Samir — can you set up the lead routing and form? Marco — sample app + benchmark script? Dana — social assets and short video scripts? Elaine — I'll coordinate release cadence and announce plan.

Samir Patel: On lead routing — I'll add fields to the form: `utm_campaign`, `source_tier`, `expected_tokens_per_call` and hook them to HubSpot. For gating, we should add an optional checkbox: "Request a Dedicated demo" to flag enterprise intent.

Dana Ortiz: Visuals: 3 x 15s clips (one for each tutorial) + one 60s overview. I'll draft storyboards and share in Figma by EOD Friday.

Marco Chen: repo structure idea: `/tutorials/snackloop/01-latency`, `/02-cost`, `/03-private` with simple README + `docker-compose` for local. Keep deps minimal.

Elaine Walker: KPIs: blog pageviews, tutorial video completions (50% watch), webinar signups, signups->paid conversions within 30 days, and lead score distribution. We'll set benchmarks after first week.

Priya Nair: Webinar format: 35m demo + 15m Q&A. Save one or two deep-dive breakout sessions for advanced ops (batching, quantization) for the follow-up email.

Samir Patel: PublishingBot: please create a calendar event for launch and schedule the webinar page when assets exist.

PublishingBot: Event created: "Snackable Tutorial Loop launch" on 2026-05-14 10:00 PDT — landing page placeholder: https://redwood.example/landing/snackloop (status: draft).

Dana Ortiz: Quick ask — can we get a short benchmark chart export (png + raw csv) from Marco so I can animate for social?

Marco Chen: yes. I’ll add `bench_output/latency_chart.png` and `bench_output/latency.csv` to the repo tomorrow AM.

Elaine Walker: Action items: Priya (blog + webinar outline) due Tue, Marco (sample app + bench scripts + assets) due Wed AM, Dana (social + video storyboards) due Fri EOD, Samir (form + HubSpot routing) due Wed EOD. I'll do final checklist and announce in #general on launch day.

Priya Nair: noted. Also proposing a small prompt-eval harness for the blog so we can show a before/after quality check when recommending quantization or batching. Helps reduce objections.

Samir Patel: one more — include a UTM in the sample app README links so devs demo-ing locally replicate tracking: `?utm_source=repo&utm_campaign=snackloop`

Elaine Walker: perfect. If no blockers, we move forward. Any legal/compliance flags for the gated webinar content?@Dana @Priya check with security about using real customer logs in examples — we should sanitize.

Dana Ortiz: will confirm with security. If we need to scrub examples, we'll use generated datasets.

Marco Chen: one tiny technical note — recommend default `sequence_length=128` in examples to match bench and cost claims.

Elaine Walker: Great. Thanks team — I'll post the kickoff doc and assign the tasks in Asana. :rocket: 

Samir Patel: :thumbsup:
